title: Responsive density engine and token mapping for cost canvases
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Create a cohesive density engine and token mapping that lets the Console adapt component density and spacing across: cost canvases, rollout rails, and compact dashboards. This ticket covers: token naming conventions, responsive token breakpoints, component-level overrides for compact/expanded states, Figma library updates, and a short prototype to validate microinteraction rhythm under three data densities. Rationale: Teams keep creating ad-hoc spacing variants for each dashboard which increases visual drift and implementation bugs. The density engine will be an opinionated layer (tokens + small API surface) that front-end can consume via CSS custom properties or style tokens. Scope: tokens and docs + Figma components and 1 prototype page + cross-team consistency review. Out of scope: runtime batching logic, backend telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Token schema defined with clear naming for scale/density/intent
Figma library updated with density variants for 12 core components
Prototype demonstrating three density states in cost canvases (sparse, default, dense)
Implementation spec with CSS token mapping and example SCSS variables
Sign-off from Design Lead and Frontend Engineering on consistency trade-offs
design_notes: Prefer intent-based token names (eg --space-inspect, --space-condensed) over pixel-only tokens to improve future-proofing
Introduce 'density' axis with values: sparse | default | dense; map to spacing, font-size scale, and hit area adjustments
For rollout rails, keep metric line-height tied to token so that compact state doesn't truncate labels
Accessibility: ensure compact states maintain 44px minimum touch targets for primary actions; where unavoidable, provide alternative keyboard flow
Provide migration guide for teams using older pixel tokens with a 2-release deprecation window
decisions: Adopt intent-first namespaced tokens: rwd.space.inspect, rwd.space.condensed, rwd.type.body-compact
Three density breakpoints mapped to CSS custom properties and exported from Figma tokens plugin
Component variants in Figma will be single-source with boolean variant flags (compact=true/false) to reduce combinatorial explosion
Avoid introducing new colors in this ticket; focus strictly on spacing/typography/hit areas to minimize scope
tradeoffs: Using intent names reduces explicit pixel control for engineers but improves semantic clarity across rollouts
Boolean compact flags in Figma simplify handoff but require disciplined constraints to avoid inadvertent overrides
Maintaining minimum touch sizes in dense mode may cause tighter visual rhythm; we prioritize accessibility over absolute density
